scope: HBQ initVehicle/start compared with CBE bootstrap and late native crew cleanup
findings: HBQ init marks InitDone before delayed enabled check. If disabled after the five-second delay it exits before installing Local handler; start independently checks enabled/local/alive and spawns driveAssist, unstuck, crewHold and unflip workers. Do not copy source flags as proof of later re-enablement or quiescence.

CBE installs native cleanup init/Local callbacks after settings readiness independently of tactical enablement; normal discovery and tactical scheduling remain separate. This scoped review does not prove all runtime toggle paths.
Crew can enter or change seats after the five-lookup locality observation window without another locality edge. Existing actual-seat cleanup helper was not reached by those events.
implementation: Install guarded per-vehicle GetIn and SeatSwitched native handlers in existing LandVehicle init.
Offer entered/swapped actors to DrivingRecoveryCrewAdopt. Its actual local driver/effective-commander/local LandVehicle checks reject passengers, static weapons and remote callers.
Reuse finite observation epoch/window and deduplicated pending release ticket. No reverse, command replay, movement deadline renewal, world query or recurring worker is added.
cost: Two native event-handler slots per LandVehicle in addition to existing Local handler; event-only callbacks. Actual runtime budget remains unmeasured.
remaining: Event timing, delayed crew setup, same-owner seat switching and subsystem-off cleanup require physical normal/HC tests.
Receipt delivery after the finite lookup window without another native event remains unsupported.
Actual effective-commander reassignment without a seat/locality event is not covered by these new callbacks.
Whole-HBQ controller parity and measured5%median/10%p95 remain incomplete.
